dedupe_keys.name: niosh mining disasters table us mine incidents with five or more deaths 1839 to present

description: This NIOSH table lists mining disasters in the United States from 1839 to the present, where a disaster is an incident with five or more deaths. Each row gives the date, mine name, city and state, number killed, product mined, accident type, mine type and mining sector, and the table can be exported to Excel or PDF. It is published by the Mining Program of the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health. Coverage is national across coal and other mining sectors. It is free online without registration; the page states no licence, as usual for US Government works. Caveats: some counts exceed those in the Mine Safety and Health Administration database because federal inspector deaths from OSHA records are included, the table rows load through a script and were not displayed to the cloud reader, and the underlying accident reports are held in the MSHA Academy library in Beckley, West Virginia, on request. For simulation it gives a long record of catastrophic mine accidents, classed by accident type, for estimating the frequency and severity of mining disasters that disrupt coal and mineral supply chains and for testing emergency response scenarios. It is related to the MSHA mine data record in this catalogue, which holds accident and injury reports for all mines.
